title: A handoff is not a completion claim
subtitle: A tested review gate keeps work blocked until its modeled findings are cleared, and blocks again when verification fails.
evidence_label: Three isolated control-plane tests passed; synthetic fixtures, real HTTP handlers, in-memory state.
source_revision_basis: The three tests ran on 2026-09-19 at 18:54 UTC in a checkout whose file tree is identical to this commit on the private repository's main branch; the three test files match it by SHA-256.
amended: 2026-09-22: added finding_status, resolution_timestamp_recorded and status_change_event_recorded to the "Mark finding fixed" stage, added the "Mark final verification passed" stage, and corrected two typos in supporting_assertions. The added assertions were read from the same tests' source; no tests were rerun. 2026-09-23: added source_revision and its basis, taken from the private test receipt; no tests were rerun.

workflow_assertions.result: One dispatched reviewer slot and mailbox reference are created.
The repeated read adds no duplicate message-received event.

supporting_assertions.case: Bare review approval with no rationale, references or finding
Update another task's finding through the wrong task URL
Update through the finding's own task URL

claim_limits: allowed=true means no modeled blocking finding or blocked/failed verification status; it is not task completion or proof of correctness.
The illustrated stages summarize assertions across existing isolated tests, not a captured single production session.
No production database, real agent session, provider behavior, external task write or deployment was exercised.
Resource-to-task binding is covered; the empty-membership scope fixture does not prove production authentication.
An evidence reference, rationale or finding satisfies the anti-rubber-stamp shape check; truth and quality of that evidence remain unproved.
Only open high/critical findings are blocking under the finding rule; candidate findings have a separate optional gate not exercised here.
Routing records a finding-routing event; it does not execute a fix or establish that an agent performed one.
The supporting task-scope check includes a successful in-scope update; it is not only a rejection test.
The published summary contains selected safe assertions. Application source and the full private verification receipt are not published here.
